item.title: Unearthed: El-Sayed called for repealing law that made sex without disclosing HIV status a felony
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed once called Michigan's HIV criminalization law "hateful" and "discriminatory," a stance now under scrutiny in his Senate race.
item.content:encoded:
Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed once called for repealing a Michigan law that made it a felony for people who knew they had HIV to have sex without first informing their partner — a position he is standing by eight years later as he campaigns in one of the nation's most competitive Senate races

As he unsuccessfully ran for Michigan governor in 2018, El-Sayed repeatedly took aim at the law. The law carried a prison sentence of up to four years for people who knew they were HIV-positive and engaged in sexual penetration without first informing their partner of their HIV status.

"You should not be criminalized for a disease. That is absolutely wrong. It’s hateful. It’s discriminatory, and we can, as a state, do better. You can count on me for that," El-Sayed said as he ran for governor.

MICHIGAN STUDENT CONFRONTS EL-SAYED OVER IRAN STANCE

Fast-forward eight years and El-Sayed, an epidemiologist and a former health director for Detroit-anchored Wayne County, is battling former Republican Rep. Mike Rogers in the midterm race to succeed retiring Democratic Sen. Gary Peters. The showdown in Michigan is a must hold for the Democrats as they try to win back control of the Senate from the GOP.

As he ran for the 2018 Democratic gubernatorial nomination — a contest he lost to now-two-term Gov. Gretchen Whitmer — El-Sayed's campaign website stated, "Repeal HIV/AIDS criminalization laws and the exclusion of transgender Michiganders from state Medicaid."

When asked in 2018 if he supported the decriminalization of HIV through legislation that would create two levels of misdemeanors, El-Sayed said at the time, "One of the big things that we have to recognize about HIV is that no disease can be illegal. The continuing forward of these laws on the books stigmatize people with the disease."

SIX FORCES THAT COULD HELP REPUBLICANS DEFY HISTORY IN THE MIDTERM ELECTIONS

Whitmer also supported changing the law, which dated to 1988, saying as she ran for governor, "It’s wrong to criminalize sickness, which is what this law has effectively done. It absolutely should be revisited."

The law was reformed in early 2019. The revised statute limited the felony provisions to vaginal and anal intercourse involving an intent to transmit HIV or cases in which HIV was actually transmitted, reduced certain non-transmission offenses to misdemeanors and protected medically suppressed people from prosecution under the law's reckless-disregard provision.

"Abdul supports the bipartisan reform bill that passed in 2019 through a Republican legislature that eliminated the discriminatory laws on the books," campaign spokesperson Roxie Richner told Fox News Digital. "As a public health professional, Abdul has fought to support programs that stem the spread of diseases, including HIV."

Richner added that "the Trump administration has completely exacerbated this crisis by defunding the organizations and programs that do frontline care to prevent transmission and exposure in the first place. In the US Senate, Abdul will fight back against Donald Trump and RFK Jr’s attempts to dismantle our public health infrastructure and ensure all Americans have access to the care they need."

DEMOCRACY ’26: STAY UP TO DATE WITH THE FOX NEWS ELECTION HUB

El-Sayed also stands by his past comments on fighting discrimination aimed at those with HIV.

Last week, as he landed an endorsement from the Human Rights Campaign, a leading LGBTQ advocacy group, El-Sayed highlighted that if elected to the Senate, "I’ll fight to ensure every Michigander can live without discrimination and never have to wonder whether their rights will still be there tomorrow."

El-Sayed, who narrowly edged more moderate Democratic Rep. Haley Stevens in August in a contentious primary that further exposed the rift between the party's left-wing and establishment factions, would become the nation’s first Muslim senator if elected.

He has made support for "Medicare for all" a major component of his campaign. El-Sayed has also called for abolishing Immigration and Customs Enforcement and has been a vocal critic of Israel during its war against Hamas, characterizing Israel’s actions in Gaza as "genocide" against Palestinians.

item.title: Packers tight end Tucker Kraft hears boos from Lambeau Field fans and offers tone deaf response
item.description: Tucker Kraft called Lambeau Field booing "pretty disappointing" after the Green Bay Packers' blowout home loss to the Atlanta Falcons Thursday.
item.content:encoded:
Green Bay Packers tight end Tucker Kraft dropped a couple of passes during Thursday night's blowout loss to the Atlanta Falcons, which was indicative of his team's stunningly inept performance that caused the Lambeau Field crowd to boo the home team.

And Kraft was stunned by that.

Hurt by that.

No, not the loss. The booing.

BROWNS PICK DESHAUN WATSON AS THEIR STARTING QB DESPITE HOME CROWD BOOING AND HIS '17 AWAY GAMES' COMMENT

"Yeah it’s pretty tough," Kraft told reporters huddled around his locker stall. "You know, like everyone pictures Lambeau Field and not boos. I don't picture boos. I picture my home stadium. That's tough. It's pretty disappointing."

Friends, it is 2026 not 1966.

So, the Packers of Vince Lombardi, Ray Nitschke, Jim Taylor, Herb Adderly, Willie Wood, Jerry Kramer and the other men who made this franchise a beacon of excellence and toughness and turned Green Bay into Titletown are a long-ago memory.

Now, we've got these Packers, who lost their last five games last season, and collapsed in giving up a big lead to lose their season-opener this season, and then lost their home-opener against the Falcons on Thursday night.

And these guys are complaining about being booed.

FROM THE CHARGERS TO THE COLTS AND FALCONS, WHICH OF THE NFL'S EIGHT WINLESS TEAMS ARE ALREADY IN PANIC MODE

These Packers got run out of Lambeau Field by a previously winless team. So, darn right, the fans booed.

But Kraft, who heard the boos, is tone deaf.

"It's pretty disappointing," Kraft continued. "It's not gonna help us win. Like, I don't know, I don't know what people think that's gonna rally us or something like that.

"But, you know, we're grown men. We're mentally strong enough, capable enough to get back on the field and play ball. Um, but, probably much easier with the 70,000 people behind us rather than opposing us."

This is not the way, Tucker Kraft.

You just signed a $75 million contract extension. You got $26.5 million of that in a signing bonus. So, just for signing your name on the document you collected more money than most of your fans make in their lifetimes by a multiple of 100.

And you don't understand why they're unhappy when you and your teammates do not perform? You don't picture boos?

Fans didn't picture their team giving up 27 unanswered points to the Falcons.

Fans didn't picture their team rushing for a grand total of 17 yards. Or the defense giving up 242 rushing yards.

And nobody pictured Kraft suddenly talking about them as if Deshaun Watson suddenly took over his body.

The stunning part is that Kraft is one of the most stand-up guys on the Packers. He is a tough player. He fights back from injuries. He is not a victim.

But this was full-on soft victim mentality.

To be fair: This is not all Kraft talked about after the game. He talked about rallying and even admitted to not playing "to my standard."

But that's the minimum expected reaction after what fans have witnessed going back to December of 2025.

What no one expects is a team leader in any way lecturing fans that showed their displeasure the only way they really can. Those people pay to be in the stadium and have the right to express their displeasure in this manner.

Some fans at other venues throw beer bottles.

Kraft, his teammates and coaches have been giving the fans plenty to be displeased about.

And the only proper response to the question about being booed on Thursday night was, "We deserved it and will try to do better."

item.title: More Americans than ever now have a positive view of socialism, new poll says
item.description: A new Gallup Poll shows 43% of Americans view socialism positively, with independents surging from 37% to 45% as big business approval plummets.
item.content:encoded:
More Americans than ever view socialism positively, according to a Gallup poll released Wednesday, as 43% view it positively for the first time since 2010.

Gallup asked respondents if they have a positive or negative image of socialism, capitalism, free enterprise, big business and small business in the poll conducted in August. Fifty-five percent of Americans view capitalism positively.

The poll's findings show a significant drop in how Americans view big business, which is down 14 points from 2010, free enterprise down 9 points and capitalism down 6 points. Small business is the only category that hasn't lost any support.

SOCIALISM SURGES AMONG DEMOCRATS AS PARTY LEADERS REJECT DSA AGENDA: ‘PACK OF FOOLS’

The increase in socialism’s positive rating through 2025 was largely due to the views of Democrats, rising from 50% in 2010 to 66% last year. However, this year's increase is due to political independents, according to Gallup, whose positive rating jumped from 37% in 2025 to 45%.

This year's findings show 65% of Democrats view socialism positively, compared with 14% of Republicans.

FOX NEWS POLL: SQUEEZED BY COSTS, FRUSTRATED VOTERS TURN TO THE DEMOCRATS

Lucas Holtz, a senior political advisor at Third Way, told Fox News Digital in a statement, "The Gallup poll isn't evidence of Americans embracing socialism—it's evidence that Americans are rejecting the economic status quo. When we look a single layer beneath to ask whether voters support socialist policies, support completely collapses."

"Working-class Americans are pissed about the costs of everyday life and the economy, but it's off base to think that a majority of Democrats and independents would back wholesale DSA socialism," Holtz continued.

JOE MANCHIN SAYS HE WOULD NEVER SUPPORT A SOCIALIST CANDIDATE, WARNS AGAINST 'CRAZY' POSITIONS

Holtz pointed to a Third Way poll that found Democrats and Democratic-leaning independents prefer "capitalism with guardrails" over socialism by 24 points.

"Echelon Insights also ran a poll and found that socialism is 33 points underwater with independents. And they found that a whole lot of DSA-aligned policies would make voters less likely to back a candidate. Abolishing police and prisons: 73% less likely (77% among independents). Ending all immigration detention and deportations: 43% less likely (42% among independents). Government ownership of major transportation and energy infrastructure: 39% less likely (44% less likely among independents)," Holtz said.

The Gallup poll found that views of the economic systems differed by age group.

Adults aged 18 to 34 view socialism more positively than capitalism, 57% vs. 43%, and those aged 55 and older view capitalism more positively than socialism, 65% vs. 34%.

VANCE WARNS THERE WILL BE A 'SOCIALIST PRESIDENT IN THIS COUNTRY' IF GOP DOESN'T FIX ECONOMY FOR YOUNG PEOPLE

Adults ages 35 to 54, however, rate socialism and capitalism about the same.

A professor of political science at Northeastern University, Costas Panagopoulos, told Fox News Digital, "For Independents, whose views are driven least by partisan attachments, perceptions about socialism are gaining in favorability in part because they feel betrayed, overlooked or neglected by modern American capitalism."

SOCIALISM’S RISE INSIDE THE DEMOCRATIC PARTY NOW THREATENS THE AMERICAN DREAM

Gallup's summary of its poll read, "Capitalism, free enterprise and especially big business are viewed less positively than they once were, while socialism has gained ground. Those changes have been most pronounced among Democrats and younger adults, but this year's uptick in socialism's appeal reflects a novel shift among independents."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

The poll comes amid a rise in socialist political candidates across the country, some of whom have won primary elections.

After being sworn into office this year, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani, a democratic socialist himself, also helped propel three congressional candidates, Brad Lander, Claire Valdez and Darializa Avila Chevalier, to victory in New York's primary in June.

item.title: Supreme Court allows Trump admin to use federal voter eligibility database during appeal
item.content:encoded:
An order issued Friday by the Supreme Court temporarily allows the Trump administration to move forward with a mass voter verification system.

The emergency order allows states, for now, to use the Department of Homeland Security program, called Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements, or SAVE, in their efforts to verify the eligibility of voters on their rolls. 

Because existing law blocks most states from systematically purging voters from their rolls within 90 days of an election, the immediate impact of Friday's order on the upcoming midterms is likely limited, the Associated Press reported. States' use of the SAVE program is voluntary.

The court’s order puts on hold a federal judge’s June ruling that had deemed the Republican administration’s recently revamped version of SAVE illegal. U.S. District Court Judge Sparkle L. Sooknanan had blocked the use of the tool, saying it violated Americans’ privacy rights and could result in voters being wrongly removed from the rolls.

A federal appeals court declined to pause Sooknanan's ruling, prompting the administration's appeal to the Supreme Court.

An executive order signed by Trump had directed the creation of a federal voter registration list and imposed new restrictions on eligibility for voting by mail as part of the administration's broader effort to combat voter fraud.

The SAVE program was created under an immigration law mandating that DHS help federal, state and local agencies prevent government benefits from going to noncitizens. The Trump administration last year moved to significantly expand its search abilities. Since then, at least 67 million registrations have been scanned through the program, but critics, the AP says, worry it could end up purging valid voters from the rolls.

This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.

Fox News Digital's Ashley J. DiMella and the Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Dozens of pledges found covered in food in sweltering frat basement as police investigate alleged hazing
item.description: Roughly 30 partially clothed young men were found in a sweltering basement during rush week at the Alpha Epsilon Pi house in Madison, Wisconsin.
item.content:encoded:
Police responding to an anonymous hazing tip at a fraternity in Madison, Wisconsin, found roughly 30 partially clothed young men packed inside a sweltering basement, covered in food, condiments and other liquids – with several showing signs of being physically assaulted, authorities said.

The Madison Police Department said officers were dispatched to the Alpha Epsilon Pi (AEPi) house along Langdon Street around 8:20 p.m. Wednesday, where a thermostat in the basement was set to 81 degrees, creating hot and humid conditions.

The vast majority of those inside were 18 years old, police said. Officers declared the gathering unlawful before escorting everyone outside and checking the pledges for injuries and incapacitation.

MIAMI SECRET SERVICE AGENT CHARGED IN NEAR-DEADLY FRATERNITY HAZING, OFFICIALS SAY

Police said the chapter is not recognized or accredited by the University of Wisconsin-Madison and was terminated by the university more than a decade ago. Alpha Epsilon Pi's national organization, however, told Fox News Digital it still recognizes the Madison chapter.

Madison Police Capt. Kipp Hartman said Thursday that he observed what appeared to be fresh redness and marks potentially consistent with being struck, but did not see any open wounds.

FORMER MICHIGAN HOCKEY PLAYERS ALLEGE COACHES IGNORED YEARS OF ABUSIVE HAZING RITUALS

Hartman added that he was not aware of anyone being transported for medical treatment.

Police said fraternity president Brayden J. Klein and vice president Samuel N. Vane, both 20, were arrested on hazing and disorderly conduct allegations and taken to the Dane County Jail.

PENN STATE COCAINE BUST NETS 14 ARRESTS OVER ALLEGED PLEDGE COKE-CUTTING ‘INDOCTRINATION' RITUALS

Hartman said both alleged offenses are misdemeanors and the Dane County District Attorney's Office will review the case.

Investigators are still working to determine exactly what happened inside the house, and Hartman said officers encountered inconsistencies while interviewing those who were there.

"We had limited cooperation," Hartman said.

Officers obtained statements from those at the scene, but Hartman said some "did not align with what everybody else's statements were," raising concerns for investigators.

The incident came during rush week at UW-Madison. Hartman said he believes everyone involved was a university student.

Alpha Epsilon Pi describes itself as "the world’s Jewish college fraternity," with chapters on more than 150 college campuses in four countries.

Jonathan Pierce, the fraternity's chief communications officer, confirmed to Fox News Digital that AEPi recognizes its Madison chapter and said members remain subject to the national organization's health and safety policies.

"AEPi Headquarters takes the allegations involving our Pi Chapter in Madison, Wisconsin, extremely seriously," Pierce said in a statement. "We will cooperate fully with the authorities investigating this matter."

Pierce said any member found responsible for criminal conduct would be expelled and that AEPi would support prosecution.

"Hazing is a betrayal of everything our fraternity stands for. There is no place for it in AEPi," the statement read. "No exceptions. No excuses. We educate our members about their responsibility to ‘Be Your Brothers’ Keeper.’ This is not an optional value."

item.title: The SEC might have more headliners, but the Big 12 has the most underrated matchup of week 4
item.description: Oklahoma State and West Virginia both own ranked wins, and Saturday's Big 12 showdown could determine who has the inside track to a playoff berth.
item.content:encoded:
We have one hell of a college football weekend on our hands, folks.

If you haven't done so already, open up another tab and take a quick look at the slate for this Saturday.

I'm sure your eyes will be drawn to plenty of action in the SEC, as the league has two of the more intriguing match-ups in terms of national relevance.

The number one team in the land, Texas, will travel to Knoxville to take on a dangerous looking Tennessee team, while the team with perhaps the best resume in the country, Ole Miss, takes a trip to The Swamp to play the Gators.

My point is that Saturday will feature wall-to-wall action and could end up being one of the best weekend slates of the season.

But one game that isn't getting the shine it deserves is taking place in the Big 12.

It doesn't feature a ranked-on-ranked match-up, and is occurring at the same time that LSU and Texas A&M are set to square off, but the showdown between Oklahoma State and West Virginia will be must see television.

NEW AP POLL TOP 25 PUNISHES OHIO STATE, OKLAHOMA, OREGON, TEXAS JUMPS TO NO 1 AFTER BIG COMEBACK

For starters, both teams have a ranked win on their resume, something many programs around the country can't say they have, as the Mountaineers took down a top-25 Virginia squad while the Cowboys toppled mighty Oregon in week two.

The match-up will feature a couple of great coaches on opposite ends of the spectrum, both stylistically and in terms of where they are in their career.

OKLAHOMA STATE MIGHT HAVE KNOWN WHICH PLAYS OREGON DUCKS WERE RUNNING DURING UPSET WIN

Oklahoma State has Eric Morris roaming their sidelines, and if you've been paying attention to me at all in the past year, you know how much I like this guy.

Morris, the young up and comer, is an air raid disciple, and it shows in his team's offensive splits.

The Cowboys rank top ten in total offense and have the best passing offense in the Big 12 thanks to Morris' system and quarterback extraordinaire Drew Mestemaker.

On the other side you have Rich Rodriguez, and if that name sounds familiar, it's because he's on his second tour in Morgantown.

His first go around as West Virginia's head coach was wildly successful, featuring plenty of explosive offenses and BCS Bowl victories, and it looks like he's picked up right where he left off.

The Mountaineers have one of the best rushing offenses in the country, ranking in the top three nationally in rush yards per game.

This game will be an explosive one when either offense is on the field, as the scoreboard operator better hope he's up for the challenge.

The stakes will be plenty high as well, because the winner of this game will have an early inside track on making it to the Big 12 title game and potentially upsetting Texas Tech en route to a College Football Playoff berth.

You will want to be tuned in when these two square off in the Mountain State.

If it's not the main game on your TV, I implore you to at least go picture-and-picture or just go buy a second monitor (they're cheap these days).

Don't let the fancy numbers next to teams like LSU and Texas A&M distract you from the fact that this could be the most entertaining game of the weekend.

Miss it at your own peril, and don't say I didn't warn you.

item.title: Fighter jet pilots eject moments before fiery crash in Wales
item.description: Video captures two Royal Air Force pilots ejecting from a Hawk T2 training jet moments before a fiery crash near Anglesey in Wales on Wednesday.
item.content:encoded:
A video captured the moment two Royal Air Force pilots ejected from a training aircraft before a fiery crash in Wales.

The Royal Air Force (RAF) said the incident involving a Hawk T2 aircraft happened near Anglesey on Wednesday after the pilots departed the RAF Valley base in the northwestern part of the country.

"Both pilots are doing well, they are in extremely good spirits and expected to make a full recovery," the RAF said in a statement. "A formal investigation into the circumstances surrounding the incident is now underway and as a precautionary measure, the RAF has temporarily paused Hawk T1 and Hawk T2 flying operations."

BLOODIED, EJECTED MARINE CORPS PILOT SEEN CALM AND COLLECTED AFTER WASHINGTON CRASH DESTROYS AIRCRAFT

Footage taken by local resident Danni Jones and obtained by Storyful shows the pilots parachuting through the air after a fireball erupted in the Welsh countryside.

The RAF said on its website that the Hawk T2 "is a high-performance, 2-seat training jet equipped with advanced avionics and synthetic radar to simulate front-line combat aircraft like the Typhoon."

PILOT EJECTS AS F-35 CRASHES AT MCAS MIRAMAR, SPARKING FIRE

"Used primarily by the RAF for advanced jet training, it prepares pilots for complex tactical environments," it added.

The cause of Wednesday's crash was not immediately clear.

"RAF Valley on Anglesey is home to No 4 Flying Training School, responsible for training the UK's next generation of world-class fighter pilots," according to the RAF. "Aircrew are also trained at RAF Valley for mountain and maritime operations throughout the world."

item.title: '80s star Tiffany steps into dream role after leaving Hollywood behind
item.description: Tiffany reveals her Off-Broadway role in "Spandex the Musical" fulfills a lifelong dream she put on hold when "I Think We're Alone Now" took off.
item.content:encoded:
'80s pop icon Tiffany is stepping back into the spotlight as she fulfills a dream she had prior to becoming a teen idol.

The 54-year-old singer, who rose to fame in 1987 after her song "I Think We're Alone Now" became a massive hit, made her Off-Broadway debut in "Spandex the Musical" last week.

During a July interview with People magazine, Tiffany reflected on why taking the stage felt like a "true full-circle moment for me."

'80S POP STAR TIFFANY EMBRACES QUIET NASHVILLE ROUTINE AFTER LEAVING CALIFORNIA BEHIND FOR GOOD

"Before music came into my life, I was a dancer and an actor, and those dreams were put on hold when ‘I Think We’re Alone Now’ took off and my recording career began," she said.

Tiffany, whose full name is Tiffany Darwish, launched her career with the now-legendary Shopping Mall Tour '87, performing free concerts at malls across the country beginning in June 1987. The grassroots campaign helped turn the then-15-year-old into a teen sensation before she became a chart-topping artist.

In September 1987, Tiffany's cover of Tommy James and the Shondells' 1967 hit "I Think We're Alone Now" climbed to No. 1 on the Billboard Hot 100 less than two months after its release and made her a household name.

"I Think We're Alone Now" was the second single released from her self-titled debut album. She followed up with "Could've Been," the third single released from "Tiffany," which also topped the Billboard Hot 100. In addition, the album produced her Beatles cover "I Saw Him Standing There," which peaked at No. 7 on the Billboard Hot 100, and "Feelings of Forever," which reached the No. 50 spot.

At 16, Tiffany became the youngest female artist to top the Billboard 200 with a debut album. She went on to headline her first major tour in 1988, with New Kids on the Block opening for her before the boy band's own meteoric rise.

However, Tiffany's chart dominance proved difficult to sustain. While her 1988 sophomore album, "Hold an Old Friend's Hand," was certified platinum by the RIAA and produced the Top 10 hit "All This Time," it fell short of matching the success of her debut. As the teen-pop landscape shifted in the early 1990s, her third album, "New Inside," failed to gain commercial traction.

RICK MORANIS, CAMERON DIAZ AND LINDSAY LOHAN AMONG STARS WHO LEFT FAME BEHIND BEFORE RETURNING TO HOLLYWOOD

In 1993, Tiffany released her fourth album, "Dreams Never Die," which was issued only in Asian markets. Afterward, Tiffany largely stepped back from the mainstream music scene to focus on raising her son Elijah, whom she shares with her ex-husband, makeup artist Bulmaro Garcia. The two were married from 1992 to 2003.

In the early 2000s, Tiffany left Hollywood behind and moved to Nashville. During a 2023 interview with Fox News Digital, she explained why she decided to embrace a simpler life in Tennessee.

DOLLY PARTON'S PATH FROM NASHVILLE NEWCOMER TO BILLBOARD'S NO. 1 COUNTRY MUSIC ARTIST OF ALL TIME

"I came to Nashville for the first time when I was 10," the California native recalled. "I’ve been coming back ever since. I love being out in the country – I’m a country girl at heart. I’ve toured all over the world and this place has always been home for me. There’s just something about coming home to my little ranch… I’ve never looked back."

Since the days of her teenage stardom, Tiffany has continued to tour and release music as an independent artist. She has also made appearances in movies and television shows and starred in several reality TV series.

During a June interview with Fox News Digital, Tiffany detailed how she spent the past several years building a culinary brand that combines her love of cooking, entertaining and connecting with fans. Through her platform, "Let's Food With Tiffany," she offers recipes, virtual cooking experiences and food-focused events that showcase the same energy and creativity that made her a pop sensation.

Earlier this year, Tiffany released her second cookbook, "POP LIFE: The Ultimate ‘80s Kitchen Encore," which she created with Las Vegas celebrity chef Alicia Shevetone. "POP LIFE: The Ultimate ’80s Kitchen Encore" followed her first cookbook, "Breakfast with Tiffany," which she released independently.

In July, Tiffany announced that she would make her New York theatrical debut in "Spandex the Musical," in which she plays Linda Gustafson, a housewife who competes in the fictional 1988 Crystal Light National Aerobics Championship.

"I’ve always believed the right role would find me, and the moment I read the script, I knew Linda was that character," she told People magazine at the time.

"Just as Linda discovers a new passion through aerobics that changes her life, I’ve found exciting new passions beyond music through my ‘Pop Life’ cookbook, ‘Let’s Food With Tiffany’ events, and now returning to acting on stage," she continued. "It’s a reminder that it’s never too late to reinvent yourself."

GET ENTERTAINMENT SCOOP DELIVERED RIGHT TO YOUR EMAIL BY CLICKING HERE

"Spandex: The Musical" is a 10-day limited Off-Broadway engagement which runs through Sept. 27. After each performance, Tiffany performs "I Think We're Alone Now" during the curtain call.

"There are so many wonderful parallels between Linda’s journey and my own, and I’m thrilled the producers have even woven in some fun Tiffany Easter eggs that I know longtime fans are going to love," she told People.

item.title: Social worker sues after she says she refused to conceal students’ gender transitions from parents
item.description: Jeanette Martinez claims Albuquerque Public Schools forces staff to hide students' gender transitions from parents, violating her First Amendment rights.
item.content:encoded:
A New Mexico social worker is suing Albuquerque Public Schools (APS) over a policy she says requires school personnel to conceal students' gender transitions from their parents.

The Center for American Liberty filed a lawsuit in federal court on behalf of Jeanette Martinez, a licensed clinical social worker. Martinez said the district is forcing her to keep parents in the dark regarding their children's social gender transitions, violating her First Amendment rights to free speech and religious freedom.

Martinez, who has worked as a social worker for more than a decade, supports special-education students at Atrisco Heritage Academy High School. Her role requires routine communication with parents regarding academic, behavioral and special-education needs. As a practicing Christian, Martinez said her deeply held religious convictions prohibit her from lying or intentionally concealing the truth.

"They even decided how they were going to introduce his new name to his classmates," Martinez added, noting that school officials also discussed training first-grade students on how to interact with a classmate identifying as the opposite gender.

Under APS Procedural Directive PJ30, staff are instructed to use a student's preferred name and pronouns for internal records, documents and interactions. However, when communicating with parents, unless the student or parent has specified otherwise, staff are directed to use the student's legal name and the pronoun corresponding to the student's gender assigned at birth.

FIRST ON FOX: SCHOOL LIED, HID DAUGHTER'S GENDER TRANSITION UNDER DISTRICT POLICY, PARENTS ALLEGE

According to the lawsuit, Martinez now faces internal investigation, disciplinary action or potential termination if she refuses to comply with the directive.

TRUMP DOJ EXPANDS RELIGIOUS LIBERTY PROTECTIONS AFTER MAJOR SUPREME COURT RULINGS

"It's damaging. It's horrible. It doesn't work. It's unimaginable, to be honest," Martinez said.

Albuquerque Public Schools spokesperson Martin Salazar told Fox News Digital that the district does not comment on pending litigation. However, district guidance notes that the policy is intended to foster a safe learning environment and protect student privacy.

item.title: 'Red carpet for a despot': Trump's lavish Xi welcome collides with GOP anti-communism message
item.description: Republican senators criticized President Donald Trump's lavish Washington summit with Xi Jinping, warning against red carpet treatment for China's leader.
item.content:encoded:
As President Donald Trump’s summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping comes to its end, some Republicans aren’t happy with the red carpet treatment the face of the Chinese Communist Party (CCP) received.

"Quite frankly, had the White House asked me for advice, I would have suggested the president not invite Xi Jinping to Washington for such a lavish welcome here in the United States of America, based on all of the troubling issues we have with President Xi and the Chinese Communist Party," Sen. Roger Wicker, R-Miss., said.

Wicker, who chairs the Senate Armed Services Committee, has been one of the more vocal Republicans about his disdain for the meeting, which kicked off Wednesday afternoon when Trump met Xi at Joint Base Andrews — the first time a president has met with a foreign dignitary there since 2015.

BIPARTISAN DUO WANTS TO REMIND CONGRESS, TRUMP OF CHINA'S 'ATROCITIES' AHEAD OF XI VISIT

The White House argued in a statement to Fox News Digital that Trump was returning the sentiment to Jinping after his visit to Beijing earlier this year. 

"President Xi hosted President Trump in China for a historic summit this summer, and President Trump is reciprocating his hospitality by welcoming the Chinese delegation for a reciprocal visit this week," White House spokeswoman Anna Kelly said. "The President will forge relationships with anyone in order to advance our national interests and make good deals for the American people." 

It comes as Republicans are running to hold onto power in the Senate. They departed their midterm convention in Dallas earlier this month with a rallying cry: "Common sense versus communism," as progressive candidates surge across the country.

The convention was designed to remind voters that while his name is not on the ballot, Trump’s agenda is. But his meeting with Xi, optically, runs afoul of that.

"I mean, the president campaigned on an anti-China policy," Sen. Thom Tillis, R-N.C., said. "You go look at those MAGA rallies and look at everybody cheering when he said he's gonna take it to China."

"Any time we roll out the red carpet for a despot from Russia, or a despot from China, I feel the same way," he continued. "It's kind of not good."

GOP FACES BRUTAL MIDTERM HEADWINDS AS REPUBLICANS PAINT ELECTION AS ‘COMPETITION WITH COMMUNISM’

Sen. John Cornyn, R-Texas, said he was not "enthusiastic" about the summit, and said that China, Russia, Iran and North Korea were an "axis opposed" to the U.S.

"I hope the president's clear-eyed about who he's dealing with," Cornyn told Fox News Digital. "I mean, he tends to call some of these dictators friends, and they're no friend. I can guarantee."

Some Republicans are willing to accept that a meeting between Trump and Xi is a necessary step in building a relationship between the two superpowers, even with the lavish nature of the summit.

"I think there's value in being able to talk with your adversaries," Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., told Fox News Digital. "And I think, in this case, you know, our two countries, the biggest economies in the world, have a symbiotic relationship."

Sen. Steve Daines, R-Mont., was invited to attend the dinner after spending years working in China before running for office.

Daines told Fox News Digital that he understood his colleagues’ apprehension, but that the U.S. and China, and particularly Trump and Xi’s relationship, had to work.

TRUMP-XI SUMMIT COULD HOLD KEY TO LOWER GAS PRICES, GOP CHAIRMAN SAYS

"This relationship is too big to fail, and it's only appropriate that President Trump and his team extends respect to Xi Jinping, and it's really reciprocal to what they did for President Trump back in May when they showed him great respect when he showed up in Beijing," Daines said.

Still, that doesn’t mean Republicans have to like it.

"It is one of his strengths, his ability to sort of win individuals over with hospitality," Sen. Kevin Cramer, R-N.D., told Fox News Digital. "He's in the business. So I don't, again, I'm not gonna second guess it. You know, I hate seeing it at a personal level, but I trust his instincts on it."

Lawmakers hoped that the two-and-a-half-day summit would yield deals on the artificial intelligence (AI) race, trade deals that would end the trade war between the U.S. and China and for Xi to use his influence to get oil and natural gas flowing through the Strait of Hormuz again.

Trump kept tight-lipped about the nature of their bilateral meeting in the Oval Office on Thursday, but so far, Xi has promised two new pandas while the president is mulling allowing Chinese electric vehicles to be built in the U.S.

Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., took no issue with the meeting, but hoped that Trump would see through any smokescreen Xi deployed.

"I just suggested, and I don't think he will — the president's a pretty good judge of character — not to believe President Xi’s bulls---, because he's lying. Particularly about helping Iran, and Xi could get the Strait open immediately if he wanted," Kennedy told Fox News Digital.

item.title: Sunny Hostin's holdout juror claim complicated by conflicting reports from infamous 1991 murder trial
item.description: Sunny Hostin claimed she was the holdout juror in the NYC cannibal killer trial, but co-jurors told multiple outlets the holdout was an unemployed man.
item.content:encoded:
"The View" co-host Sunny Hostin said on-air Tuesday that she was a holdout juror in the 1991 murder trial of Daniel Rakowitz, known as the "Butcher of Tompkins Square Park," but contemporaneous accounts offer conflicting descriptions of the jury's deliberations.

During a discussion of the holdout juror in the Lindsay Clancy trial, Hostin recounted her experience on the Rakowitz jury, prompting news outlets to compare her account with reporting from 1991.

"And apparently, several jurors questioned afterwards said one holdout juror was principally responsible for preventing them from returning a guilty verdict," Hostin said Tuesday while citing a 1991 New York Times report. "That was me," she added.

While Hostin served on the Rakowitz jury, the New York Post reported that other contemporaneous accounts identified an unemployed man as the principal holdout. The Post wrote that "jurors told The Post, Newsday, the Daily News and the Associated Press that the actual holdout was an unemployed man who wanted to keep the trial going so he could continue getting paid by the court for his civic duty."

LINDSAY CLANCY HOLDOUT PRAISED AS 'AMERICAN HERO' BY LAWYER WHO SAYS HE REPRESENTS HIM

"He was unemployed and liked the $15 a day and the three free meals," juror Valerie Holmes told Newsday after the verdict, according to contemporaneous coverage.

The Post also cited a law enforcement source familiar with the case who said, "We were told that the juror who held out was a man. There was no other description."

Another factor, The New York Post said, was that "Hostin was quoted as a juror on the case in multiple news clips at the time — but she did not identify herself as the holdout, nor did any of the fellow jurors who talked to the press after the trial. Her statement to Newsday from the time even seemed to contradict her story."

"We had to compromise. But it is obvious to me he butchered the body, and he literally got away with murder. He attempted to commit the perfect crime," Hostin, then identified as Asunción Cummings, told Newsday.

LINDSAY CLANCY HOLDOUT JUROR ‘LOOKED AT THE CASE AND HE MADE THE CALL,’ HIS BROTHER SAYS

The Post noted that "one Newsday article from 1991, however, suggested that there were two holdout jurors who pushed the other 10 to find Rakowitz not guilty or risk a hung jury."

When contacted by the Post, Hostin reiterated that she was a holdout, saying, "I was. I was the holdout juror."

NewsBusters Associate Editor Nicholas Fondacaro reported on the story as well, noting that while multiple sources had written about an unemployed male holdout juror, multiple sources had also said that there were two holdout jurors.

"Outside the courtroom at State Supreme Court in Lower Manhattan, jurors said that at the end of deliberations, 10 members of the panel wanted to convict Rakowitz of murder, but two others insisted he was mentally ill and should not be held responsible for Beerle's death. They said the 10 decided to defer to the two holdouts to avoid a hung jury," the Newsday article said.

The news article had gone on to indeed mention Hostin, under the surname of Cummings at the time.

"The jurors said that one of the two panel members seeking the insanity acquittal wanted the deliberations to drag on for days. 

"'He was unemployed and liked the $15 a day and the three free meals. He liked that we were arguing on and on,' said juror Valerie Holmes, a 35-year-old clerk,'" the article continued. "'We had to compromise,' said Asuncion Cummings, a 22-year-old paralegal. 'But it is obvious to me he butchered the body and he literally got away with murder. He attempted to commit the perfect crime.'"

Fox News Digital reached out to "The View" for comment.

item.title: Ex-Dem insider blows lid off fundraising 'gimmicks' during 2024 election: 'Pyramid scheme'

Lindy Li, a former Democratic fundraiser who switched her party affiliation over unheeded warning signs of President Joe Biden’s decline in the 2024 election, believes the party badly misallocated its fundraising, misled donors and rewarded party operatives who propped up Biden’s image.

"It was: ‘maintain this very obvious lie in return for access,’" Li recalled in an exclusive interview with Fox News Digital, referring to assertions that Biden was not experiencing cognitive decline.

Li herself would find her access completely cut off after she began questioning Biden’s physical ability to serve another four years as president. Her revelations include what then-Vice President Kamala Harris did with a historic, billion-dollar war chest.

NANCY PELOSI DENIES KNOWING ABOUT BIDEN'S DECLINE, CLAIMS THOSE WHO KNEW 'SHOULD HAVE ACTED'

For starters, Li believes that the numbers themselves weren’t what they appeared to be from the outside.

"I sincerely believe it's a pyramid scheme," Li said.

She explained how fundraisers would sometimes take credit for each other’s work. In some cases, top recruiters could effectively double-dip on work that their subordinates had done.

"When you recruit somebody, you can claim up to $250,000 of what they raise," Li said.

"In fact, you could poach other people's donors and move money around. And that is how some people reach like $10 million without actually raising a thing. It's like accounting gimmicks and machinations rather than real money. I know there were people who were double counted."

As a top fundraiser for both Biden and Harris, Li worked closely with top donors, high-profile members of the party and the Democratic National Committee (DNC). Li described how she had a front-row seat for many of the party’s spending decisions.

Li recounted that most of the Harris campaign's spending went through four large media contracting companies. These contractors, Li said, collected enormous fees and received over half a billion dollars. The companies that were listed in her book included Media Buying & Analytics, Gambit Strategies, Bully Pulpit Interactive and Dupont Circle Strategies.

CARVILLE SHREDS DEMS' 2024 AUTOPSY, SAYS HARRIS CAMPAIGN WAS 'MOST INEFFECTIVE $2 BILLION EVER SPENT'

"This tsunami of money represented about 70 percent of the campaign’s expenditures in the final days, enriching a handful of well-connected consultants while the broader effort collapsed," Li wrote.

In interviews with Fox, Li described how the payments to the firms came partially as off-the-top fees.

"The vast majority of the money raised went into TV ads. And so... You know, people talk about 10% for the big guy. Okay, but I actually think the bigger grift is 15% for the big grift for these media people. They get 15%, 15 points off of hundreds of millions of dollars. You can do the math," Li said.

"The consultants get the money, the consultants that are hired by the campaign, and they're friends of the candidate or friends of Jen O’Malley-Dillon. It's a very incestuous process," Li said, referring to the Harris campaign chair.

In addition to the media companies and the lucrative contracts they paid out, Li believes that the party focused too much on expenses that didn’t advance the campaign while, in her view, neglecting strategic opportunities.

"$350,000 a night slapping her face in the Las Vegas sphere, spending that money on Gulfstream so they wouldn't have to fly commercial, spending it on Ritz-Carlton hotels. I mean, that definitely happened because the National Finance Committee was hosting its final meeting there. Spending its money on tote bags," Li said.

"None of that in Philadelphia," she added, referring to the critical electoral center in Pennsylvania — a state that had been projected to be a pathway to victory in 2024.

HARRIS BACKS RELEASING DNC'S 2024 ELECTION AUTOPSY DESPITE LEADERSHIP BURYING REPORT

Part of what shocked Li was how brazen the party had been with the money she helped raise. She also expressed disbelief at the message the party spun to voters who had contributed their earnings in hopes of "saving democracy," a refrain Biden used to convince voters to side with him over President Donald Trump.

"Some people forked over their life savings. Like people were liquidating their savings on the hope that they were saving the country. They absolutely did, and I truly believe that they donated $2.5 billion over seven weeks, not so much primarily because of Kamala's strength as a candidate, but rather their hatred for Trump and their fear of Trump," Li said.

"Everyone knew, everyone played along."

item.title: Trump revives Supreme Court immigration showdown after Hochul pardon torpedoed first case
item.description: The Trump administration asks the Supreme Court to decide whether criminal aliens in ICE detention are entitled to bond hearings during removal.
item.content:encoded:
The Trump administration is asking the Supreme Court to revive a major immigration fight over whether criminal aliens can be held without bond throughout removal proceedings or are entitled to a hearing when their detention drags on.

Solicitor General John Sauer asked the Supreme Court on Monday to take up Genalo v. D.C., reviving a constitutional fight the justices had been set to hear this term in Genalo v. Black before New York Democratic Gov. Kathy Hochul’s pardon rendered that case moot.

At the center of the dispute is D.C., a Dominican national who is facing removal after a criminal history that includes drug trafficking and domestic violence charges. He had previously been removed from the United States on six occasions, according to ICE.

Federal law requires certain criminal aliens to remain in custody while their deportation cases play out. But the Second Circuit has ruled that if they are detained for too long, they are entitled to a bond hearing at which the government must make the case for keeping them in custody.

BLUE STATE GOVERNOR'S PARDON OF CONVICTED FELON TORPEDOS A MAJOR SUPREME COURT IMMIGRATION FIGHT

Other appeals courts have taken different approaches, leaving the Supreme Court with a nationwide split over what constitutional protections apply.

"So the rights of these criminal aliens who were being detained, whether or not they're entitled to a bond hearing as of right now depends on which jurisdiction they happen to fall in," Michael Morley, a Florida State University law professor, told Fox News Digital. "And so the government is asking the Supreme Court to set one uniform interpretation for the entire country."

The Trump administration's petition is procedurally unusual because Genalo v. D.C. is still pending before the Second Circuit. Sauer is asking the Supreme Court to intervene before the appeals court issues its decision.

"Rather than making the court go through those motions, you just hear this case now, hear this case directly, even before the Second Circuit has had the opportunity to rule," Morley told Fox News Digital.

The legal dispute could also determine who carries the burden when a bond hearing is required.

Under the Second Circuit's approach, the government must show that a detainee poses a flight risk or danger to the community. The administration argued that if the Constitution requires such hearings, the burden should instead fall on the detainee seeking release.

Lawyers supporting the administration argue that some detainees could delay their removal cases, then use the length of their detention to seek release on bond.

"The biggest issue that happens here is gamemanship," Chad Mizelle, chair of litigation at the America First Policy Institute and a former acting associate attorney general, told Fox News Digital.

"A lot of times these aliens will file multiple applications for asylum, withholding removal. They'll get new attorneys, switch out attorneys, ask for continuances, ask for delays," Mizelle said. "So all of a sudden they've been in detention now, six, seven, eight months, completely of their own making."

FEDERAL APPEALS COURT DEALS BLOW TO TRUMP DEPORTATION AGENDA

Mizelle argued that if prolonged detention eventually gives a detainee the right to seek bond, it could create an incentive to stretch proceedings long enough to reach that point.

"They would switch out attorneys. They would make frivolous filings regarding asylum, regarding withholding of removal. They would ask for delays and continuances upon delays and continuances," Mizelle said. "They'll do everything they can to try to stretch this out, six months, seven months, eight months, file a habeas petition, say that they're entitled to a bond hearing, and then if they are released, abscond."

Carrie Severino, president of the Judicial Crisis Network, similarly described the additional litigation as "a foot dragging, sand in the gears exercise."

"This is attempting to stall, attempting to run out the clock or just, you know, the question is whether there even is a clock," Severino told Fox News Digital.

She pointed to cases such as Demore v. Kim, in which detainees themselves sought additional time during proceedings before later challenging the length of their detention.

OBAMA, BIDEN JUDGES DRAW FRESH FIRE AS TRUMP’S IMMIGRATION COURT CLASHES HEAT UP: ‘ALMOST IMPOSSIBLE’

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

"So, it's often a situation where people are playing both sides of it," Severino said. "But they're asking for more time on different things, but then at the same time complaining that the whole process is taking too long."

However, Severino cautioned that she could not speak to the motivations of every detainee.

The Supreme Court has previously upheld mandatory detention during removal proceedings, but Morley said the high court has left open the constitutional question now at the center of the administration's petition.

"This is a question that the [Supreme Court] itself went out of its way, you can say, to leave open for adjudication in a future case," Morley said.

The administration is now asking the justices not to wait for another one.

"You wanted to resolve this case. Here's another case that presents the same exact question that lets you resolve the circuit split this term," Morley said. "So basically, substitute this case for the moot case."

Fox News Digital reached out to the Justice Department for comment.

item.title: Ed Sheeran concertgoers warn artists about sharing political views: 'You're going to alienate' fans
item.description: Ed Sheeran fans at his Philadelphia concert warned artists that political statements alienate audiences. Sheeran's Gillette Stadium shows, planned for the weekend, were canceled due to weather.
item.content:encoded:
Several fans who attended Ed Sheeran’s concert in Philadelphia last weekend after Macklemore was dropped for making "Free Palestine" comments, warned other artists that if they make political statements, they will alienate half of their audience.

The "Bad Habits" singer was expected to play his second and third concerts since the controversy this Friday and Saturday at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough, Massachusetts, which is owned by Robert Kraft. 

However, both shows have since been canceled.

"Due to the severe weather warnings in place in Boston and across New England throughout the weekend and following consultation with local officials, we have made the difficult decision to cancel the Ed Sheeran concerts at Gillette Stadium," tour promoter Messina Touring said in a statement on Friday. "The decision was made with the safety of fans, staff and everyone involved in the shows as the top priority."

ROBERT KRAFT, GILLETTE STADIUM BOOT MACKLEMORE FROM ED SHEERAN TOUR OVER ‘FREE PALESTINE’ RANT

Previously, the New England Patriots owner allegedly threatened to cancel the concerts at his venue if Macklemore wasn’t taken off the tour, according to the "Thrift Shop" rapper.

Macklemore also claimed Kraft got other stadium owners to agree to not allow Sheeran to play at their venues if the rapper was still with his tour.

"The fact that they’re forcing Ed Sheeran to have an opinion is not right," one woman told Fox News Digital outside last Saturday’s concert. "He wants to stay in the middle – if you have an opinion, that’s fine, but you’re going to alienate at least 50% of your population, and it causes unrest."

She said the "Shape of You" singer "just wants to do his music and play his music, and people want to enjoy it. They want to get away from it, and I don’t feel as though they should have to worry about this stuff when they come to a concert."

GORILLAZ FRONTMAN DAMON ALBARN HOLDS UP PALESTINIAN FLAG DURING SHOW AFTER MACKLEMORE TOUR REMOVAL

We all come from different backgrounds, different understandings, and trying to group all those together and say, ‘You only have to have one opinion of everything,’ I think it kind of makes it rough for everyone to kind of just enjoy their lives and enjoy what makes them happy."
